chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ibn Muskan who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the meat of donkeys, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade eating it on the day of Khaybar.
He said, And I asked him about eating horses and mules, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade it, so do not eat them unless you are compelled to do so.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating donkey, horse, and mule meat in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between the permanent prohibition of domestic donkey meat, rooted in the Prophet's decree at Khaybar, and the conditional prohibition of horse and mule meat, which permits consumption during necessity (idtirar). Shia jurists utilize this distinction to derive rulings on the permissibility of various animals based on the degree of prohibition and the presence of exigency, reflecting the practical application of prophetic tradition in dietary law.
